one_line: A money-planning workspace that lets ChatGPT prepare bounded recommendations for user approval.
what_it_does: Tracks balances, bills, goals, minimum reserves and funding limits, then lets an agent calculate and stage a recommendation without moving real funds.
leverage_rationale: The shared, current financial state, approval gate, single-use exact recommendation, and invalidation after changes make structured agent access materially safer and more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies current workspace reads, limits, exact approval, one-time application, and cancellation when state changes.
Frame sheet shows a dedicated money workspace and structured setup flow, though not a legible agent call.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and the onboarding/workspace flow is visibly implemented, but the submitted frames do not demonstrate the end-to-end agent recommendation and approval path.
execution_evidence: Frames show onboarding, workspace creation, natural-language situation entry, and financial planning UI.
About text describes balance projections, bills, goals, currencies, and approval semantics.
impact_rationale: Personal budgeting and constrained goal funding are concrete needs, and the product addresses them with a safer planning workflow while clearly limiting claims to local records rather than bank transfers.
impact_evidence: About text identifies balances, bills, savings goals, reserves, and repeated calculations as the target problem.
Frames show a polished financial onboarding and workspace flow.
creativity_rationale: The combination of conversational financial planning with explicit stale-state invalidation and human approval is a thoughtful, credible angle on agent-assisted budgeting.
creativity_evidence: Single-use exact recommendations and invalidation on changed financial state are distinctive interaction rules.
The product frames ChatGPT as an explainer/planner rather than an autonomous money mover.
usability_note: Clear onboarding and approval framing; the core agent workflow is not legible in the video frames.
red_flags: No visible tool invocation or completed recommendation in the reviewed frames.
standouts: Strong safety boundary around approval, exactness, and stale state.
advance_reason: Strong finance use case and unusually meaningful safety/state semantics despite incomplete visible agent evidence.

one_line: A cross-museum gallery and exhibition builder with an AI co-curator.
what_it_does: Searches museum APIs, saves artworks into a personal gallery, and lets an agent sequence works and write exhibition narratives and wall cards.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates over structured saved artworks and exhibition state, enabling sequencing, annotation, and narrative generation in a shared gallery rather than merely clicking search UI.
leverage_evidence: About text names eight WebMCP tools for search, draft exhibitions, sequencing, and captions.
Frames show museum search/grouping UI and artwork results, but no legible tool call.
execution_rationale: The search-to-gallery concept is coherent and visibly packaged, but frames mainly show landing/search/gallery states rather than a completed agent-built exposition.
execution_evidence: Frames show Museum Media Grouper, search/filter controls, and populated artwork cards.
About text describes three live museum sources, Cloudinary gallery storage, and human review.
impact_rationale: Art lovers, students, and educators have a credible use for cross-institution discovery and personalized exhibitions; the product directly supports exploration and interpretation.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets searching major collections, private galleries, and curated exhibitions.
Visible artwork result grid supports the discovery premise.
creativity_rationale: Cross-museum aggregation plus an agent as co-curator and narrative exhibition builder is a fresh, memorable interaction model pursued beyond a simple search tool.
creativity_evidence: Agentic exposition builder and human-in-the-loop curation are central to the concept.
The project turns museum APIs into a personal storytelling workspace.
usability_note: The gallery/search interface is understandable; agent-generated exhibition completion is not clearly shown.
red_flags: No explicit readable tool invocation or completed exposition in the visible frame sheet.
standouts: Distinctive cultural/educational use of agentic curation.
advance_reason: Strong creative and audience fit with meaningful structured-agent potential.

one_line: MODE lets an agent personalize a dense website’s presentation to each user.
what_it_does: Uses natural-language preferences to reshape a fictional storefront’s layout, visibility, typography, contrast, and sorting while preserving the site’s facts and actions.
leverage_rationale: The core product is shared human-agent control over presentation state: typed capabilities let an agent reliably transform a site in ways general UI driving would be brittle, slow, and hard to persist.
leverage_evidence: About text describes agent-controlled display preferences stored in cookies and a clear separation between site-owned facts and user-owned experience.
Frames show storefront states with an agent/tool side panel and visibly altered browsing context.
execution_rationale: The concept, storefront demo, and personalization framing are coherent and appear intentionally implemented across multiple visible states; exact transformations are somewhat small in the contact sheet.
execution_evidence: Frames show a functioning retail catalog, hero, product grid, scrolling states, and an auxiliary interaction panel.
About text gives concrete accessibility, decluttering, sorting, and persistence behaviors.
impact_rationale: Personalized presentation can address accessibility, attention, and shopping preferences for broad classes of users without changing trusted content or functionality.
impact_evidence: About text gives concrete low-vision, ADHD, price-conscious, and preference-driven scenarios.
Frames visibly show a dense storefront being viewed alongside the personalization surface.
creativity_rationale: The principle that the website owns facts while the user owns experience is a genuinely strong interaction concept, connecting agents to adaptive accessibility rather than chat-only assistance.
creativity_evidence: MODE treats presentation as an agent-editable preference layer rather than a fixed site theme.
The project combines ordinary-language intent, persistent preferences, and developer-exposed capabilities.
usability_note: The storefront and personalization framing are clear; small frame text limits detailed verification of the transformed result.
red_flags: Exact tool names and before/after changes are not legible in the contact sheet.
standouts: Strong human-owned presentation model and accessibility angle.
advance_reason: One of the clearest and most consequential WebMCP-native concepts in the packet.

one_line: A shared 2D/3D home-gym planner where an agent proposes layouts under physical and budget constraints.
what_it_does: Models rooms and obstacles, adds equipment from a catalog, validates clearances/access/goals/cost, and lets agent and human edit the same undoable project.
leverage_rationale: Live shared spatial state plus typed equipment, validation, and common undo/redo makes an agent substantially more capable and reliable than pixel-driven manipulation of a 3D editor.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly says manual and WebMCP actions share commands, state, validation, and undo history.
Frames show a rendered room editor, object inspector, and conversational/task panel.
execution_rationale: The visual editor and room model are clearly real and coherent, with a meaningful validation scope; the contact sheet does not fully prove every constraint or end-to-end agent iteration.
execution_evidence: Frames show a stable 3D room layout, side panels, and iterative editor states.
About text specifies room boundaries, collisions, clearance, access, ceiling, mounting, goals, and cost checks.
impact_rationale: Home-gym buyers face real space, safety, training, and budget constraints, and the product directly helps them reason about a concrete purchase/design decision.
impact_evidence: Pitch and description target fit-to-room, training goals, access, and budget.
Visible room editor demonstrates the relevant spatial planning surface.
creativity_rationale: The shared human-agent 3D design workflow and validation-aware collaboration are an ambitious and memorable application of WebMCP beyond text generation.
creativity_evidence: Agent edits are visible in the same spatial editor and use the same history as manual edits.
The concept combines visual design, physical constraints, and training-goal coverage.
usability_note: A conventional editor structure and visible room model suggest good usability, though contact-sheet text is small.
red_flags: Agent calls and validation messages are not fully legible in the frames.
standouts: Shared state, validation, and undo semantics are unusually well integrated.
advance_reason: High WebMCP leverage with strong visible product execution and a concrete constraint-heavy domain.

one_line: A live multi-user sticky-note board where humans and outside agents edit together and can refuse unsafe actions.
what_it_does: Synchronizes an infinite canvas across tabs, exposes board inspection and editing tools, shows agent bodies/cursors, and lets tools reject actions based on concurrent activity.
leverage_rationale: Shared live state, awareness of human activity, multi-agent concurrency, visible embodied actions, and refusal semantics are precisely the capabilities a general UI-driving agent cannot replicate comparably well.
leverage_evidence: About text describes direct tab sync, eleven tools, change queries, human activity, embodied actions, and interaction-aware refusal.
Frames show a canvas-oriented product and agent-oriented activity presentation, though fine details are small.
execution_rationale: The board concept and interaction rules are coherent, and the described concurrency/refusal model is unusually complete; frame readability limits proof of live multi-tab behavior.
execution_evidence: About text specifies React Flow, Zustand, Yjs awareness, BroadcastChannel sync, and one wrapper for animated agent actions.
Frames show a structured board/editor presentation rather than a static landing page.
impact_rationale: Teams and individuals collaborating on planning or ideation can gain value from a board where agents participate visibly and safely instead of operating in a detached chat.
impact_evidence: Pitch and description identify shared brainstorming/planning and concurrent human/agent work.
Refusal based on other participants addresses a real collaboration concern.
creativity_rationale: Embodied outside agents on a shared board, with live awareness and the ability to say no based on other actors, is an exceptionally original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The project explicitly rejects the chat-window-only agent pattern.
Visible cursors, held notes, time-based motion, and refusal-as-return-value pursue the concept deeply.
usability_note: The shared-board metaphor and visible activity are strong; multi-window proof is not fully legible in the sheet.
red_flags: Exact live synchronization/refusal sequence is not readable from the contact sheet alone.
standouts: Most ambitious multiplayer and refusal-aware agent interaction in the packet.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and creativity, with a credible shared-state implementation story.

one_line: A browser-native human-in-the-loop preflight gate for Q# quantum requests.
what_it_does: Loads and hashes a Q# artifact, compiles it locally, evaluates a deterministic policy, gates bounded simulation behind human acceptance, and exports an evidence receipt.
leverage_rationale: Progressive tool exposure, typed bounded simulation, one-use consent, and evidence binding make agent-assisted quantum execution safer and more auditable than generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies four progressive tools, state-dependent exposure, one-use consent, strict bounds, and artifact/target evidence binding.
Frames were included as product-motion evidence, but detailed labels are not available in the contact sheet analysis.
execution_rationale: The described preflight pipeline is unusually specific and internally coherent, with deterministic recommendations and local compilation; visual end-to-end confirmation is limited.
execution_evidence: About text enumerates artifact loading, SHA-256, pinned Q# WASM compilation, policy outcomes, simulation, and export.
Live/demo and public repository facts support a substantial implementation claim.
impact_rationale: Quantum developers and researchers have a credible safety/audit need before costly or consequential execution, and the product addresses it without overstating QPU access.
impact_evidence: Description identifies artifact verification, target evidence, limits, authority, and spend as the pre-execution problem.
The explicit zero-QPU/provider-credential boundary makes the value proposition credible.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to a deterministic, evidence-producing quantum preflight gate is a distinctive domain-specific interaction with meaningful safety depth.
creativity_evidence: Exactly-one recommendation policy and progressive consent tools are memorable design choices.
Evidence receipt binds human choice and measured effects to the exact artifact.
usability_note: The staged workflow should support safe review, but frame details were insufficient for a strong usability read.
red_flags: No provider execution is intentionally demonstrated; the packet relies heavily on description for the deepest workflow.
standouts: Strong evidence/audit design and bounded consent model.
advance_reason: Credible, technically distinctive safety workflow with strong domain fit.

one_line: A React SDK that makes invisible WebMCP work visible and collaborative in the product UI.
what_it_does: Provides deeplink onboarding, connection status, live work states, action history, permission prompts, and an in-frame agent activity rig.
leverage_rationale: It does not add domain capability, but it materially changes WebMCP’s human-agent collaboration by exposing connection, progress, history, and permission in the live product rather than hiding calls.
leverage_evidence: About text defines an SDK covering the full multiplayer session arc and argues that invisible calls fail for co-op UX.
Frames visibly show a product dashboard alongside a dark WebGPT/tools panel and interaction controls.
execution_rationale: The SDK concept is coherent and the frames show both polished product/landing surfaces and an interaction panel; exact SDK behavior is only partly visible.
execution_evidence: Frames show dashboard states, the agent/tool panel, and visible interaction affordances.
About text enumerates onboarding, connection, work, history, permission, and a simple SDK API.
impact_rationale: Teams building agent-enabled products have a real need for trust, observability, and permission UX; the audience is specialized but the pain is credible.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets developers integrating WebMCP and users who need to know whether agent work is happening.
Visible panel supports the stated in-frame observability thesis.
creativity_rationale: Framing the SDK as a camera rig for agent action and treating WebMCP as multiplayer UX is a fresh, memorable product/interaction metaphor.
creativity_evidence: The concept focuses on felt co-presence rather than hidden automation.
The full session arc and action-in-frame framing pursue the idea beyond a status indicator.
usability_note: Visibility and permission affordances are clear in the shown panel; exact integration ergonomics are not demonstrated.
red_flags: Some claims about SDK reusability and multiplayer are not independently demonstrated in the contact sheet.
standouts: Strong observability and trust layer for agent-in-product UX.
advance_reason: Useful infrastructure UX with clear visible tool/action framing.

one_line: A typed capability-discovery and decision-packet workflow for software selection.
what_it_does: Maps fuzzy software needs to capabilities, evidence, examples, bounded scope, and a staged human-review recommendation using six page tools.
leverage_rationale: The page exposes a structured capability/evidence model and stages a shared decision packet for human review; this avoids unreliable agent inference from marketing pixels and keeps uncertainty visible.
leverage_evidence: About text names six typed tools from capability discovery through stage_human_review and a shared Agent Trace.
Frames visibly show six registered tools, native WebMCP status, agent tool-call labels, and a Human-review packet.
execution_rationale: The product’s sparse interface, tool registration status, trace, and review packet form a coherent workflow, though the final decision content is small.
execution_evidence: Frames show LIVE IN CHROME/WEBMCP READY/registered-tools status and a human-review packet interface.
About text describes evidence boundaries, constraints, decision surface, and visible invocation trace.
impact_rationale: People and teams choosing software often begin with vague needs; typed evidence-backed translation can reduce research friction while preserving human authority.
impact_evidence: Description gives concrete needs such as mobile public data, offline workflows, and replacing manual processes.
The visible review-packet endpoint aligns with a real procurement/discovery handoff.
creativity_rationale: The concept turns a website into an evidence-aware capability model for agents, not a generic chatbot, and makes human review the convergence point.
creativity_evidence: Explicit tools-not-pixels thesis and bounded proof boundaries.
Agent trace and staged human-review packet are integrated into the interaction model.
usability_note: The editorial UI clearly communicates agent readiness and review staging; detailed packet readability is limited by frame scale.
red_flags: The visible packet contents are too small to verify a complete recommendation.
standouts: Strongest explicit visual evidence of native tool calls and human-review output.
advance_reason: High leverage with unusually direct visual evidence of the intended WebMCP workflow.

one_line: A shared cloud architecture canvas where humans and agents design and safely modify infrastructure.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect live architecture, analyze cost/resilience, propose changes, require approval, preview cost, execute visibly, and rollback/undo changes.
leverage_rationale: A live graph with shared resources, dependencies, cost, policies, simulation, approval, rollback, and visible execution is far beyond reliable generic browser driving; the agent operates on structured architecture state.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies 20 tools operating on the same React Flow state, strict schemas, approval, cost previews, pause/cancel, rollback, and undo.
Frames show CanvasOps messaging about live product state, assistant interaction, visible action, and result cards.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and ambitious, with a visible architecture/assistant narrative and detailed safety semantics; the small frame sheet cannot verify all 20 tools or rollback end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Frames show a consistent dark CanvasOps presentation with canvas/assistant/action-result surfaces.
About text describes architecture components, validation, cost previews, approval, rollback, and implementation stack.
impact_rationale: Infrastructure design has real complexity and costly failure modes; a shared, policy-aware architecture assistant can provide credible value to developers and platform teams.
impact_evidence: Description targets cost, resilience, policies, regional failure simulation, and safe modification.
The live architecture canvas directly represents the audience’s existing workflow.
creativity_rationale: The combination of visual infrastructure graph, live agent collaboration, cost/safety gates, and reversible execution is an ambitious and memorable WebMCP application.
creativity_evidence: Intent-in/visible-action-out framing is pursued through shared canvas state.
Provision-and-pay is separated as a human-approved tool with rollback semantics.
usability_note: Visible proposal/approval/result framing supports trust; exact canvas manipulation details are too small to inspect.
red_flags: The contact sheet does not make individual infrastructure operations legible.
No real cloud provisioning should be inferred from the description alone.
standouts: Excellent structured-state and reversible-change model for infrastructure work.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and impact potential with a coherent safety-oriented workflow.

one_line: A website auditor that turns performance/accessibility findings into evidence-rich briefs for coding agents.
what_it_does: Audits a public URL with PageSpeed/Lighthouse and live-document analysis, then retains rule IDs, routes, selectors, evidence, priorities, hints, and acceptance criteria.
leverage_rationale: Structured retained audit evidence and agent-ready acceptance criteria improve the handoff substantially, though a general agent could consume a conventional report with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text details provenance, rule IDs, routes/viewports, selectors, occurrences, evidence, repo hints, and acceptance criteria.
Frames show audit/development imagery and a branded frontend analysis presentation, but no explicit WebMCP call.
execution_rationale: The audit-to-brief workflow is clearly scoped and the packaging is coherent, but frames are largely stylized montage/marketing imagery rather than a legible end-to-end product run.
execution_evidence: Frames show browser/code preview, frontend issues, SEO-style score visualization, and repeated site states.
About text explains asynchronous PageSpeed/Lighthouse plus bounded live-document analysis and prioritized recommendations.
impact_rationale: Website owners and coding agents have a real handoff problem; preserving actionable evidence can reduce wasted interpretation and improve fixes.
impact_evidence: Description identifies the gap between audit dashboards and repository-capable coding agents.
Concrete acceptance criteria and evidence provenance directly serve that workflow.
creativity_rationale: The core idea is a strong, practical reframing of site auditing as agent-ready evidence, though the category is familiar and the visual concept is less novel than the top projects.
creativity_evidence: Explicit decision to provide evidence rather than replace repository agents is a focused product insight.
Rule-level provenance and proof boundaries add depth beyond a generic SEO score.
usability_note: The proposed recommendation structure is useful; the frames do not show the actual brief clearly enough to judge interaction polish.
red_flags: Video frames are stylized and do not clearly show an agent invocation or readable audit brief.
SEO/accessibility visuals alone are not proof of the complete handoff workflow.
standouts: Evidence retention and acceptance criteria are well targeted to coding-agent workflows.
advance_reason: Credible developer workflow with meaningful evidence packaging, though visual execution evidence is thinner.
